info.bio: Dead Kennedys fue una controvertida banda estadounidense de hardcore punk, surgida en la década del 80.En 1978 en San Francisco. East Bay Ray (Raymond Pepperell Jr.) un joven enamorado del Rock and Roll y la música surf pone un anuncio buscando gente para formar un grupo. A éste responde un Eric Boucher, conocido como Jello Biafra. Biafra que al volver de Londres estaba impresionado por el punk, decidió formar un grupo cuando vio un concierto de los Ramones en Denver.

scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

podcast.title: Jello Biafra's 1979 Mayoral Campaign
podcast.body: In 1979, singer Jello Biafra ran for mayor of San Francisco as a satirical act of political protest. He finished fourth in a field of ten candidates. One of his campaign promises was to mandate that all city politicians wear clown suits, highlighting his anti-establishment views. "For example, in 1979, Singer Jello Biafra ran for mayor of San Francisco."

podcast.title: Alternative Tentacles Founding
podcast.body: The Dead Kennedys formed Alternative Tentacles, a California label, initially just to release one of their singles. They enjoyed the experience so much they decided to turn it into a full-time business, following the model of Black Flag with SST and Bad Religion with Epitaph. The label also played a key role in exporting American hardcore by developing relationships with other indie labels worldwide. "At first, they just wanted to get one of their singles out there, but they enjoyed the experience so much that they decided to turn Alternative Tentacles into a full-time business..."

xref.title: "Thatchergate" Hoax (1983-1984)
xref.body: Following the Falklands War, this anarchist musical collective created a tape known as "Thatchergate." They cobbled together speeches from Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan to create what sounded like a fake phone call between the two leaders, including a fabricated discussion about firing missiles at allies. When the tape circulated in 1983, the US State Department suspected it was KGB disinformation, and MI6 considered it a possible Argentinian intelligence operation. Its true source was not discovered until January 1984. While not a song, its samples were used in tracks by Crass and the Dead Kennedys. Crass's motivation was to expose governments as "small-minded, petty and stupid," not just corrupt or violent, and the hoax indeed embarrassed the CIA. "The band cobbled together speeches from Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan into what appeared to be a fake phone call between the two of them."

xref.title: California Hardcore Scene
xref.body: The Offspring were deeply rooted in the California hardcore scene, a fierce but small community dedicated to punk that evolved from the original 1970s punk. This music became a soundtrack for skaters and snowboarders, including bands like Dead Kennedys, The Adolescents, The Vandals, Black Flag, and Bad Religion, which was niche and rarely played on radio. "Everyone was into California hardcore. The punk that evolved out of the original punk of the 1970s. The scene was small but fierce and its adherents stuck together. And some of this music became the soundtrack for skaters and snowboarders, dead candidates, the adolescence, the vandals, black flag, bad religion, really niche stuff at the time, and certainly stuff that never made it on the radio."

xref.body: Lock Up was Tom Morello's first band after moving to the West Coast. The lineup included drummer D.H. The band ultimately dissolved by early 1991 after their debut album failed commercially and they were released from their contract with Geffen Records. "Tom's first west coast band was called Lockup."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Refusal to Change Name for Contract
xref.body: The Dead Kennedys, known for their ultra-political stance, were approached by several record labels offering contracts on the condition that they change their band name. The band found this unacceptable, as compromising their identity went against their core ethos. "The ultra-political dead Kennedys were accorded by several labels saying that they could have a contract if they would just, you know, change their name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Roadie for The Ravers, Co-founded Dead Kennedys
xref.body: Jello Biafra worked as a roadie for a band called The Ravers. Following this experience, he and East Bay Ray collaborated to form the iconic punk band Dead Kennedys. "Jello Biapro roadied for a band called the Ravers before he and East Bay Rae formed the dead Kennedys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Use of Echo and Reverb
xref.body: Scotty Moore, a guitarist in Elvis Presley's band, was known for using echo and reverb in his sound, an element admired by East Bay Ray of the Dead Kennedys. "Another hero was Scotty Moore, who played an Elvis Presley's band, and Scotty liked to use echo and reverb in his sound, something that Ray really liked."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

xref.title: Used "Thatchergate" Samples
xref.body: The Dead Kennedys incorporated samples from Crass's infamous "Thatchergate" tape into their own musical tracks. This act connected them to a significant political hoax that fooled major intelligence agencies. "samples from this tape were used in tracks by both Crasse and the dead Kennedys."
